text:
maya: Heads-up: NF4 canary rolled at 03:10 triggered a sustained throughput drop (~22%) and a ~1.8GB GPU memory spike on a subset of hosts. Noticing kernel routing flaps between 4-bit and fp4 codepaths. @eng-runtime can someone pick this up? :eyes:

tom: Oof. Observed similar on 3 hosts in us-west-2. KV cache eviction counts spiked at the same time. I captured a short perf trace.

jordan: Can you paste the flamegraph or raw perf lines? want to confirm whether it's kernel selection overhead or a bad slowpath.

tom: pasted perf snippet and short stack:```
# perf top sample
samples: 1200  cycles:u  
  runtime::select_kernel+0x4a  (libredwood_runtime.so)
  runtime::call_kernel
  nvrtc::launch_kernel
  cudnn::xxxxx
```
Memory timeline: host A: before 03:10 used 4.2GB, spike to 6.0GB after canary. KV-cache evict rate jumped x6.

maya: Also saw calibration service logs spamming warnings about quant-block mismatch. looks like NF4 fallback policy triggered a warm-up recalibration every ~30s which keeps re-allocating temp tensors.

alexa: That warm-up recalibration was a recent safety patch for edge cases in fp4->nf4 mapping. Maybe it created a race with our batching heuristic causing many small batches to hit slowpath?

jordan: Hypothesis: routing loop where a request hits nf4 kernel, fails quality check, falls back to fp4, then subsequent telemetry switches routing back to nf4 for the same model/version, causing repeated kernel swap and repeated kv-cache churn. Each swap inflates allocations.

tom: I ran `traces/alloc_trace --host usw2-03 --since 03:08 --until 03:22` and saw alternating kernel load events every ~12-40s. Attaching sanitized sequence:```
[03:09:58] load kernel nf4_k0
[03:10:10] fallback to fp4_k1
[03:10:21] load kernel nf4_k0
[03:10:33] fallback to fp4_k1
...```
This matches the throughput oscillation windows.

maya: Can we temporarily pin the canary hosts to fp4 to stop the oscillation? We should also throttle the calibration service until we have a deterministic check.

infra-oncall: I've pinned the three affected hosts to fp4 and disabled live recalibration on that group. Monitoring now.

ci-bot: Deploy/rollback note: rolled kernel pin to fp4 on twaas-canary-group-7 at 03:34 by infra-oncall.

alexa: Good quick mitigation. Next steps: need a proper fix in routing policy to avoid flip-flop. Proposed changes: 1) add a cooldown TTL after a kernel fallback to prevent immediate re-routing for N seconds, 2) make calibration idempotent (skip if calibration already running for model+host), 3) avoid full KV-cache purge on kernel swap, instead attempt in-place remap.

jordan: Agree. I can prototype cooldown + telemetry flag in the router. Need 1-2hrs. Also will add a metric for "kernel_swap_rate" per host so we can alarm before throughput drops > 10%.

tom: For the KV behavior, I tracked that our evict policy treats swapped kernels as incompatible and triggers full cache invalidation. That's probably the big cost. I'll open an RFC for a lightweight compatibility shim to reuse KV pages when quant layout matches.

maya: Can you folks add short follow-ups with numbers? For the rollback group, current TPS recovered to baseline?

infra-oncall: After pin, TPS on those hosts returned to within 2% of baseline and memory stabilized. No further spikes in the last 18m.

jordan: I'll push a canary with cooldown + kernel_swap_rate metric to a single host group tomorrow AM and collect 6h of traces. Will share dashboard link.

alexa: Also please add an integration test that simulates repeated fallback loops to catch regressions.

maya: Thanks team. Action items: jordan prototype router cooldown + metric, tom RFC for KV compatibility shim, alexa test for fallback loop, infra to keep pin/live-recal disabled for 24h and keep logs. We'll reconvene after canary traces. :thumbsup:
